extraction.name: PIQA (Physical Interaction: Question Answering)
extraction.description: PIQA is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language. Given a physical goal expressed in natural language, a model must choose the most sensible solution from two options. The dataset is inspired by instructables.com and focuses on everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through crowdsourced annotation where annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com. Annotators were asked to glance at instructions from an instructable and construct two component tasks, articulating a physical goal and a valid solution, plus a permutation of their solution that makes it invalid. The dataset was further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm to remove spurious biases.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Instructions from instructables.com, a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair, where users provide images or videos detailing each step and a list of tools required.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were given instructables as inspiration to construct goal-solution pairs. They wrote a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid 'trick' solution (subtle permutation). Qualification HITs were run prior to main annotation requiring >80% accuracy on well-formed examples. Data was collected in batches and validated by other annotators for correctness. Users with low agreement were de-qualified. Examples with low agreement during validation were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk), based on references to HITs and turkerview.com
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Examples with low agreement were removed from the data during validation. Sentence length distributions and vocabulary overlap between correct and incorrect solutions were analyzed to check for spurious biases.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple annotators validated each item; items with low inter-annotator agreement were removed
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Spacy tokenizer and GPT BPE tokenizer were used for analysis of the dataset; RoBERTa was used for evaluation but not annotation
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may reflect reporting bias, as commonsense physical properties are rarely directly reported in language. The dataset was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm to reduce annotator biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to physical commonsense knowledge expressible in language, and knowledge learned from language alone is considered insufficient for true physical understanding. Models may 'match' humans by fine-tuning on in-domain data, but this does not reflect genuine physical understanding.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance AI research toward physical commonsense understanding, which is considered critical for AI-completeness, including robots that interact with the world and understand natural language.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating and probing language representations on physical commonsense knowledge, serving as a diagnostic benchmark for physical understanding in NLP models. It can be used for testing and analysis of large-scale pretrained models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: AFLite algorithm was used to remove annotation artifacts and stylistic biases by discarding instances whose feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label. An ensemble of linear classifiers trained on random subsets was used, with 5,000 examples used to fine-tune BERT-Large to compute embeddings. Instructables were used as prompts to flatten the distribution of referenced objects and reduce reporting bias.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text was tokenized and lowercased with punctuation removed for edit distance computation. Examples were truncated at 150 tokens (affecting 1% of data). Train, development, and test folds were automatically produced by AFLite.

name.evidence: we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA

description.evidence: we introduce Physical Interaction: Question Answering, or PIQA to evaluate language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense. We focus on everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions. Our dataset is inspired by instructables.com

creator.evidence: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi

inLanguage.evidence: we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA

isLiveDataset.evidence: The dataset is further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm introduced in (Sakaguchi et al. 2020; Sap et al. 2019) which is an improvement on adversarial filtering

rai:dataCollection.evidence: annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks. They would then articulate the goal (often centered on atypical materials) and how to achieve it. In addition, we asked them to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We collect data with how-to instructions as a scaffold... annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The instructables website is a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair. In most cases, users provide images or videos detailing each step and a list of tools that will be required.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Additional HITs (not shown) were run for qualification prior to this stage and validation afterwards... annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks... Annotators had to successfully (>80%) identify which were well formed to participate in the main HIT. Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples and validated by other annotators for correctness. Users with low agreement were de-qualed.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Annotator pay averaged > 15$/hr according to both self-reporting on turkerview.com and our timing calculations.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data... Figure 4 shows a plot of the correct and incorrect sequence lengths... the two distributions are nearly identical. We also analyzed the overlap in the vocabulary and find that in all cases (noun, verb, adjective, and adverb) we see at least an 85% overlap between words used in correct and incorrect solutions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples and validated by other annotators for correctness. Users with low agreement were de-qualed.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: our goals, as tokenized by Spacy, average 7.8 words... Figure 4 shows a plot of the correct and incorrect sequence lengths (as tokenized by the GPT BPE tokenizer)

rai:dataBiases.evidence: due to issues of reporting bias, these commonsense properties - facts like 'it is a bad idea to apply eyeshadow with a toothpick' are rarely directly reported... The dataset is further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Future research, may 'match' humans on our dataset by finding a large source of in-domain data and fine-tuning heavily, but this is very much not the point. Philosophically, knowledge should be learned from interaction with the world to eventually be communicated with language.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: we hypothesize that modeling physical commonsense knowledge is a major challenge on the road to true AI-completeness, including robots that interact with the world and understand natural language.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce Physical Interaction: Question Answering, or PIQA to evaluate language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense... PIQA as a diagnostic for physical understanding: The setup of PIQA allows us to use it to probe the inner workings of deep pretrained language models

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: we use AFLite (Sakaguchi et al. 2020) to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples from the data... The AFLite algorithm performs a systematic data bias reduction: it discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label. In practice, we use 5,000 examples from the original dataset to fine-tune BERT-Large for this task and compute the corresponding embeddings of all remaining instances.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We compute edit distance over tokenized and lowercased strings with punctuation removed... we used the transformers library and truncated examples at 150 tokens, which affects 1% of the data... the train, development, and test folds were automatically produced by AFLite.
